table_title: List the recipient of TIME magazine's Person of the Year award for each year from 2000 to 2024, with the entity type (individual, group/concept, or joint selection), the lifetime cell as the source records it, and the selection number reflecting whether the recipient had previously appeared on a Person of the Year cover.
db_analog: SELECT year, choice, entity_type, lifetime, selection_number FROM time_person_of_the_year WHERE year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2024 ORDER BY year
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'Time Person of the Year' master article, accessed 2026-05-11 (re-validated 2026-05-11 during cycle-1 repair to catch two joint-selection years that rowspan extraction initially missed). Universe is the 25 yearly recipients of TIME magazine's Person of the Year award from 2000 to 2024 inclusive, as listed in the second wikitable of the master article (the canonical main chronological list of recipients; the first wikitable is a Number-of-Selections rollup by office and is not used here; the article also has multiple smaller wikitables for People's Choice and other secondary lists, also not used). The master article's chronological list covers 1927 to the current year (the live table includes 2025 'The Architects of AI' as the most recent entry; the 2000-2024 staged window is set by the user's variant-P framing and is fully within the article's coverage). Per-row cells are taken verbatim from the master table's Year, Choice, and Lifetime columns; the 'Entity Type' column is a mechanical 3-value classification derived from the Choice cell (Individual = single named person; Group/Concept = movement, profession, or anonymous-cohort label; Joint Selection = the 2 years where the source assigns TWO sub-entities to one Year cell via HTML rowspan=2 structure — 2020 'Joe Biden; Kamala Harris' and 2022 'Volodymyr Zelenskyy; The Spirit of Ukraine'); the 'Selection Number' column is taken from the source's '(N)' parenthetical suffix on Choice cells indicating repeat appearances on a Person of the Year cover (Choice with '(2)' suffix → Selection Number = 2; otherwise = 1). The 25-row universe has 15 Individual-named years, 8 Group/Concept-named years, and 2 Joint Selection years (2020 Biden+Harris; 2022 Zelenskyy+Spirit of Ukraine), reflecting TIME's editorial pattern of occasionally honoring movements, professions, anonymous figures, or paired/joint subjects alongside named individuals. Five rows have Selection Number = 2 reflecting prior cover appearances (The American Soldier was previously honored in 1950, before the 2000-2024 window; George W. Bush, Barack Obama, and Donald Trump's prior selections in 2000, 2008, and 2016 are within the window; Taylor Swift's prior cover was as part of the 2017 'Silence Breakers' group, per the master article's note 'She was noted by the magazine as the first woman to appear twice on a Person of the Year cover'). The selection is finalized in December of each year and does not change after announcement; underlying biographical facts (year of birth for individuals, death year for deceased individuals) are stable on a multi-decade horizon with the only post-snapshot update being Pope Francis's lifetime cell which the master article updated to '1936–2025' after his April 2025 death.
_extraction_notes: Original instance filling the `temporal` category gap (gap 4 → gap 3 after this staging) and adding a new Society/Media subdomain under the Society family (Society previously had 1 instance: top3_languages_per_continent under Society/Languages). Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 1 — the master 'Time Person of the Year' Wikipedia article is the canonical single source. The article's second wikitable contains the full chronological list of recipients (1927 to the current year — 2025 'The Architects of AI' is the most recent entry as of the snapshot; the staged window 2000-2024 inclusive is fully covered). Pipeline: (1) fetch the cited Wikipedia article HTML, (2) extract the second wikitable (the first wikitable is the 'Number of selections' rollup by office and is not used), (3) filter rows to Years 2000-2024 using rowspan-aware extraction — two years in this window have HTML rowspan=2 structure where the source assigns TWO sub-entities to one Year cell (2020 'Joe Biden' + 'Kamala Harris' and 2022 'Volodymyr Zelenskyy' + 'The Spirit of Ukraine'); the rowspan-aware pass collapses those into a single staged row per year with both sub-entities semicolon-delimited, (4) for each row, take Year verbatim, take Choice verbatim (stripping the '(N)' parenthetical suffix and footnote markers but preserving the entity name in its English form), record Entity Type by mechanical 3-value classification of Choice (Individual if Choice is a single named person; Group/Concept if Choice is a movement/profession/cohort label; Joint Selection if the source's HTML rowspan structure assigns two or more sub-entities to one Year — the 8 Group/Concept entries in the 2000-2024 window are 'The Whistleblowers' 2002, 'The American Soldier' 2003, 'The Good Samaritans' 2005, 'You' 2006, 'The Protester' 2011, 'Ebola Fighters' 2014, 'The Silence Breakers' 2017, 'The Guardians' 2018; the 2 Joint Selection entries are 'Joe Biden; Kamala Harris' 2020 and 'Volodymyr Zelenskyy; The Spirit of Ukraine' 2022), take Lifetime verbatim from the Lifetime column (rendering '—N/a' as '—' for groups; rendering 'Born YYYY' for living individuals; rendering 'YYYY–YYYY' with en-dash for deceased individuals — only Pope Francis in this window has the deceased form, with the source's '1936–2025' value reflecting Francis's April 2025 death; rendering 'Born YYYY; Born YYYY' for the 2020 two-individual joint selection and 'Born YYYY; —' for the 2022 individual+concept joint selection), and record Selection Number from the '(N)' suffix on Choice (5 rows have '(2)': 2003 The American Soldier (first selection 1950, outside window), 2004 George W. Bush (first selection 2000, inside window), 2012 Barack Obama (first selection 2008, inside window), 2023 Taylor Swift (first cover 2017 as part of Silence Breakers group, inside window), 2024 Donald Trump (first selection 2016, inside window); neither of the 2 Joint Selection rows has a '(N)' marker on either of its sub-entities, so both have Selection Number = 1). Result: 25 rows × 5 columns, PK on Year, 0 duplicates. Entity Type distribution: Individual 15, Group/Concept 8, Joint Selection 2. Confidence gradient is real: very-LLM-knowable rows include the major US presidents (Bush 2000/2004, Obama 2008/2012, Trump 2016/2024, Biden+Harris 2020), the canonical heads-of-state (Putin 2007, Merkel 2015, Zelenskyy+Spirit of Ukraine 2022), and the canonical technology/business figures (Zuckerberg 2010, Musk 2021); harder calibration cells include the year-specific group selections (2002 Whistleblowers, 2005 Good Samaritans, 2011 The Protester, 2014 Ebola Fighters, 2017 Silence Breakers, 2018 Guardians), the less-frequently-named honors (2009 Bernanke, 2013 Francis, 2019 Thunberg, 2023 Swift), the joint-selection structure that requires the LLM to know both sub-entities of 2020 and 2022, and the Selection Number column which tests whether the LLM knows about prior cover appearances. Group rows have '—' in the Lifetime column reflecting the source's '—N/a' rendering. Cycle-1 repair (2026-05-11): cycle-1 audit raised one BLOCKING and one NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. (a) BLOCKING — 2020 row incomplete: the source's 2020 row uses HTML rowspan=2 structure to assign both 'Joe Biden' and 'Kamala Harris' as sub-entities; the initial cycle-0 regex parsing extracted only the first sub-row (Biden) and missed Harris. On re-fetch with rowspan-aware extraction, the audit was confirmed and a same-structure issue was discovered for 2022 (Zelenskyy + The Spirit of Ukraine, which the cycle-1 auditor did not flag but which has the identical rowspan=2 issue). Resolved by combining both sub-entities into joint-selection cells: 2020 Choice 'Joe Biden; Kamala Harris', Lifetime 'Born 1942; Born 1964'; 2022 Choice 'Volodymyr Zelenskyy; The Spirit of Ukraine', Lifetime 'Born 1978; —'. Schema extension: added 'Joint Selection' as a third Entity Type value to handle these 2 rows without collapsing them into either Individual or Group/Concept. The 2022 fix is proactive (auditor did not flag it but it has the same root cause as 2020); documenting it now avoids a cycle-2 BLOCKING. (b) NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE — stale source-coverage prose: the cycle-0 narrative described the master article's chronological list as 'covering 1927-present' with an implicit '2024 as the latest' framing. On re-fetch, the live source includes a 2025 'The Architects of AI' entry. Resolved by updating temporal_note and _extraction_notes to explicitly acknowledge the source's coverage as '1927 to the current year (2025 as of the snapshot)'; the staged window 2000-2024 is unchanged but the source-coverage prose is now accurate. Net cycle-1 universe: 25 → 25 (no row count change; 2 rows changed value).
